assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology is a rare chain from basic peptide biology (proglucagon processing, incretin action, the active truncated peptide) to drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of patient impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main difficulty. Holst (incretin physiology), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and GLP-2) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide) are the most defensible basic-science trio; Knudsen is decisive for the long-acting drugs but a prize centered on the drug-development arm would need a different configuration. Joel Habener is not on the supplied list, which I note as a gap rather than resolve.
assessment.maturity: Mature: basic findings date from the 1980s-90s, clinical efficacy is confirmed by large independent outcome trials, and the therapeutic class is stable and still expanding. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether priority between Mojsov and others who worked on the peptide is fully settled is not something I can verify from the supplied text.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise the drug-development contribution (Knudsen) over one of the physiology laureates.
Long-term safety and durability of benefit are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of cytokine cascades in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade produces durable clinical benefit established the principle of targeted cytokine therapy in chronic inflammatory disease. Concept, translation and lasting impact across RA, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly drove the mechanistic work and the first clinical trials and are the clear, widely accepted pair. Other contributors (antibody engineers, the Kennedy Institute group more broadly) exist but the core credit is clean.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: more than two decades of clinical use, multiple independent agents and confirmations, and a stable interpretation. If anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Some may argue that antibody engineering and TNF cloning contributions deserve credit, which the supplied list does not address.
Prior Lasker recognition and the age of the laureates could affect timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality, now extending to autoimmune disease. This is a clear, original and clinically transformative advance.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulation design, preclinical proof), June (4-1BB construct and first durable clinical responses) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer principle and early clinical CAR work) form a plausible trio, though Eshhar and other early receptor-design pioneers are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: multiple approved products and long follow-up showing cures in some patients; limits in solid tumours, toxicity and manufacturing remain, but the core discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Contested priority of the original chimeric receptor concept versus later optimization.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, remains under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining thymus-dependent T cells and bursa-dependent B cells established the two-lineage organisation of adaptive immunity, the conceptual foundation of modern immunology and vaccine and immunotherapy design. The discovery is original and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Miller (thymus function and T lineage) and Cooper (B lineage, with the Good-Gabrielson bursa experiments) are the natural pairing; Robert Good is deceased and not eligible, and the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature and decades-confirmed. Timing is a concern only because of the advanced age of both candidates, which argues for acting soon.
uncertainties: Historical credit allocation relative to deceased contributors cannot be fully settled from the supplied text.
Whether the committee sees this as too far in the past is a judgement, not a factual uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning and characterization of IL-6 (BSF-2) and its receptor, and the development of tocilizumab, provide a clear mechanism-to-therapy story for RA, giant-cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and severe inflammation. Impact is broad and the discovery is original.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are the two central scientists for IL-6 identification and biology; the supplied credit supports a clean pair. Contributions from other groups to the IL-6 gene cloning are possible but unaddressed.
assessment.maturity: Mature: approved therapy for more than a decade, independent confirmation of IL-6 biology, and a stable interpretation. It overlaps conceptually with TNF blockade, which may make the committee prefer one cytokine story over two.
uncertainties: Overlap in message with the TNF candidate may reduce its relative standing.
Independent contributions to IL-6 cloning by other labs are not described in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining SMN2 exon 7 splicing control and developing nusinersen turned a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one and proved that antisense splicing modulation is a viable drug platform. Impact on patients is dramatic and the concept is clear.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are well matched. Contributions from Hua, Singh and others on the early ASO work are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: approval since 2016, long-term follow-up and a growing class of RNA-targeted drugs, though the platform is younger than other candidates.
uncertainties: Allocation relative to the broader antisense chemistry field is not resolved from the supplied text.
Long-term outcome durability in treated patients continues to emerge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV demonstrably prevent persistent infection, precancer and, as population data now show, invasive cervical cancer. This is a major cancer-prevention achievement of lasting public-health value.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly) and Frazer (with Zhou, who is deceased, in early VLP work) are the central names; the three are plausible but Zhou's role is a known attribution problem and Harald zur Hausen has already been recognised for the viral cause.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of population-level effectiveness data from several countries, with strong independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Contested priority between NCI, Queensland and other groups (and the posthumous role of Jian Zhou).
Overlap with the 2008 prize for HPV causation may influence perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death rather than only increased proliferation and opened the BH3-mimetic class, with venetoclax now established in CLL and AML. The concept is original and the translation is solid.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the molecular characterization of BCL-2 in lymphoma, and Vaux showed its anti-apoptotic function; Strasser is a major follow-on contributor. Competing credit from Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto, Cleary and others (some deceased) complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the science and in the clinic (venetoclax approvals), though the credit picture around the original t(14;18) and apoptosis field is crowded.
uncertainties: Crowded and partly deceased contributor set makes a fair three-person prize difficult.
Overlap with the 2002 prize on programmed cell death.
